chunks: My father - may God have mercy on him - said: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Taflisi narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hadi, from Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha (peace be upon him), from the Imam Musa ibn Ja'far, from As-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Al-Baqir Muhammad ibn Ali, from the Master of the Worshippers Ali ibn Al-Husayn, from the Master of Youth in Paradise Al-Husayn ibn Ali, from the Master of the Trustees Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them), from the Master of the Prophets Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), who said:
Do not look at the abundance of their prayers, fasting, frequent Hajj, good deeds, and their night worship, but look at their honesty in speech and the fulfillment of trust.

key_terms.طَنْطَنَتِهِمْ: Their night worship / Recitation at night

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between ritual worship and ethical character in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Transmitted through the pristine chain of the Twelve Imams in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, this hadith shifts the focus from external ritual volume to internal ethical integrity, highlighting that truthfulness and trustworthiness are the true markers of faith. This aligns with the Shia emphasis on *Sidq* (truthfulness) as a fundamental attribute of the Imams and a prerequisite for the acceptance of worship. It serves as a practical guide for believers to evaluate their spiritual state beyond mere performative piety.
